text:
When you divide the land by lot as an inheritance, you shall set apart a portion for the LORD as a holy district out of the land: twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide.[^1]

[^1]: The Hebrew does not state the unit of measure; cubits are commonly assumed. Some ancient witnesses read twenty thousand for the width.

versions.text: When you divide the land by lot as an inheritance, you shall set apart a portion for the LORD as a holy district out of the land: twenty-five thousand cubits long and ten thousand wide. It shall be holy throughout its whole extent.
versions.explanation: The word "cubits" is supplied here but omitted in verses 3, 5, and 6, which creates inconsistency. Either drop it with a footnote explaining the missing unit, or supply it consistently throughout the passage.

text: Of this, a square of five hundred by five hundred shall be for the sanctuary, with fifty cubits of open land around it.
From this district you shall measure off a section twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide, and in it shall stand the sanctuary, the Most Holy Place.

It is the holy portion of the land; it shall belong to the priests who minister in the sanctuary, who draw near to serve the LORD. It shall be the place for their houses and a holy place for the sanctuary.
Another section, twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide, shall belong to the Levites who minister in the temple, as their possession, with twenty chambers.
As the possession of the city you shall assign an area five thousand wide and twenty-five thousand long, alongside the holy district. It shall belong to the whole house of Israel.

The prince shall have the land on both sides of the holy district and the city's possession, bordering the holy district and the city's possession, extending westward on the west side and eastward on the east side, its length running alongside one of the tribal portions, from the western boundary to the eastern boundary.
This land shall be his possession in Israel. My princes shall no longer oppress my people, but shall give the house of Israel the land according to their tribes.
Thus says the Lord GOD: Enough, you princes of Israel! Put away violence and plundering, and do what is just and right. Stop dispossessing my people, declares the Lord GOD.
You shall have honest scales, an honest ephah, and an honest bath.
The ephah and the bath shall be of the same measure: the bath a tenth of a homer, and the ephah a tenth of a homer. The homer shall be the standard for both.
The shekel shall be twenty gerahs; twenty shekels plus twenty-five shekels plus fifteen shekels shall be your mina.
This is the offering you shall present: a sixth of an ephah from each homer of wheat, and a sixth of an ephah from each homer of barley.
The required portion of oil, measured by the bath: a tenth of a bath from each kor—a kor is ten baths, that is, a homer, for ten baths make a homer.

versions.text: The required portion of oil, measured by the bath: a tenth of a bath from each kor—for ten baths make a homer, since ten baths are a homer.
versions.explanation: The clause עֲשֶׂרֶת הַבַּתִּים חֹמֶר first defines the kor (ten baths = a homer) before the confirming clause. As it stands, "for... since..." makes the sentence read as a pointless repetition and stumbles when read aloud.

text: And one sheep from every flock of two hundred from the well-watered pastures of Israel, for a grain offering, a burnt offering, and peace offerings, to make atonement for them, declares the Lord GOD.
All the people of the land shall be bound to bring this offering to the prince in Israel.

It shall be the prince's duty to provide the burnt offerings, the grain offering, and the drink offering at the festivals, the new moons, and the Sabbaths—at all the appointed feasts of the house of Israel. He shall provide the sin offering, the grain offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offerings, to make atonement for the house of Israel.
Thus says the Lord GOD: In the first month, on the first day of the month, you shall take a young bull without blemish and purify the sanctuary.
The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering and put it on the doorposts of the temple, on the four corners of the ledge of the altar, and on the posts of the gate of the inner court.
You shall do the same on the seventh day of the month for anyone who has sinned unintentionally or in ignorance. So you shall make atonement for the temple.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, you shall observe the Passover, a feast of seven days, during which unleavened bread shall be eaten.
On that day the prince shall provide a bull as a sin offering for himself and for all the people of the land.
During the seven days of the feast he shall provide as a burnt offering to the LORD seven bulls and seven rams without blemish, daily for the seven days, and a male goat each day as a sin offering.

versions.text: During the seven days of the feast he shall provide as a burnt offering to the LORD seven bulls and seven rams without blemish, one each day for the seven days, and a male goat daily as a sin offering.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew לַיּוֹם שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים means "daily, for the seven days" — seven bulls and seven rams each day, not a single animal per day. The current rendering imposes an interpretation that reduces the totals and conflicts with the plain sense of the text.

text: As a grain offering he shall provide an ephah with each bull and an ephah with each ram, along with a hin of oil for every ephah.
In the seventh month, on the fifteenth day of the month, at the feast, he shall provide the same for seven days: the same sin offering, burnt offering, grain offering, and oil.
